title: Which operation? Word problems
examples: When should I draw a picture for a word problem?
Can you give me a two-step problem about animals?
Is it always addition when I see the word 'more'?

explain.say: Today we learn how to pick the right math operation. Sometimes words are tricky to read.
Sometimes you need to draw a picture to help you think. Drawing helps you see the problem better.
A two-step problem means you must do two math jobs. You solve one thing, then use that answer for the next step.

items: Step 2: Use the answer for the next step.

explain.say: Look at this problem. Three apples and two more apples. You should draw three circles and two more circles. Then you count them all.

faq.q: If the problem talks about 'left' or 'take away', is it always subtraction?
faq.a: Usually, yes, 'take away' means you are subtracting. You can also use drawing to check this idea.

faq.q: Do I always have to draw a picture for every word problem?
faq.a: No, drawing is a helpful tool, but sometimes just reading carefully is enough. It is best to try drawing first.

faq.q: What is the difference between one-step and two-step problems?
faq.a: A one-step problem needs only one operation to solve it. A two-step problem needs you to solve two separate operations in order.
asks: How many steps are in a two-step problem?

faq.q: If I see 'altogether', does that always mean addition?
faq.a: Yes, 'altogether' usually means you need to add things up to find the total. It is a strong clue for addition.

faq.q: If the problem is about sharing equally, what operation should I use?
faq.a: Sharing equally means you are dividing the total into equal groups. This tells you to use division.

facts: Addition combines groups to find a total amount.
Subtraction finds the difference between two numbers.
Multiplication is repeated addition of the same number.
Division is splitting a total into equal groups.

quiz.say: Sarah had six stickers. Her friend gave her four more stickers. How many stickers does she have now?
quiz.why: You combine the two groups of stickers, so you add six and four to get ten.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you subtracted instead of adding the stickers together.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you put too many zeros in the answer.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only counted the first sticker.

quiz.say: Maria had twelve cookies. She gave four cookies to her brother and then shared the rest equally among her two friends. How many cookies did each friend get?
quiz.why: First, you subtract four from twelve to get the remaining cookies. Then, you divide that amount by two to share them.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you only did the first step and stopped there.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you forgot the final step of sharing the cookies.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only divided the initial twelve cookies by two.
